scope: Whole backend under the user's heavy setup (mic+speaker transcription with Google, translation, OCR, VR UI on the GPU path, VRChat running), dev-fast, Quest 3 / 150%. py-spy 0.4.0 record --nonblocking --threads 60 s at 200 Hz (Python stacks only) plus Windows per-thread CPU over the same 60 s.
conclusion: No remaining hot spot is a Rust candidate: the largest is model inference inside onnxruntime (already native). Fixed in Python: isFrameBlank samples every 4th pixel; OSC uses BlockingOSCUDPServer (one receive thread). Not changed: the OCR detector itself (thread count, interval, GPU provider are product decisions). Whole-process CPU did not drop in the second run because OCR text recognition was running; per component, the blank check left the OCR thread and OSC no longer starts a thread per packet.

after_fixes.note: Same setup, VRCT restarted with the fixes (VR mirror: exact min==max uniform check; desktop: sampled mean/var; OSC: BlockingOSCUDPServer). OCR read frames on 39/40 and 29/29 ticks, and this time also ran text recognition (candidate=2 ocr=2), so total OCR work was larger than in the first run.
